_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.310

Removes the ten-second wait at peak pressure on small cuffs. Initial timed
inflation stops at its cutoff, performs one 2.5-second sealed pump-off settle,
then starts deflation. GUI, standalone and the bench harness count this
interval once. Regular, Smart Const and High Max share the transition.

No deflation PID gains, feedforward, valve limits or calibration changed.
Remaining controller and pulse-rejection research is separate from this fix.

Device D wrist/syringe verification: ten-minute seed 213 bench run completed
all six cycles with 100% Arduino telemetry delivery; 328,750 NI samples retained
with zero gaps/backtracks. Cutoff to deflation was 3.05–3.17 seconds in the
bench harness. Six actual phase checks measured 4.06–4.49 seconds in the GUI
and 2.55–2.80 seconds in the firmware macro. These include one sealed settle;
GUI command-dispatch overhead remains. Phase checks intentionally stopped
after entry and are not full protocol trials.

Startup deflation rate overshoot and slow CVP rates remain unqualified;
completion is not a claim of corrected PID or pulse-preservation performance.

Physical CVP descent is still sluggish after phase entry: Arm/Wrist needed
8.83 / 6.94 seconds for a sustained 2 mmHg fall from their post-cutoff peak.
The software peak hold is removed; that remaining response is a separate issue.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
